page.layout: One printed page (1042) with one column of text, the canons set centred and in roman numerals; no marginal notes on this page. Below the text, at the right, the catchword INDEX. At the far right edge, a narrow cut-off sliver of the facing page with small marginal notes, mostly unreadable.

main_text.p: Delictum personæ non debet in detrimentum Ecclesiæ redundare.
Rationi congruit, ut succedat in onere, qui substituitur in honore.
In argumentum trahi nequeunt, quæ propter necessitatem aliquando [?]uut concessa.
Nemo potest plus iuris transferre in alium, quam sibi competere dignoscatur.
In toto, partem, non est dubium, contineri.
In generali concessione non veniunt ea, quæ quis non esset verisimiliter in specie concessurus.
Qui contra iura mercatur, bonam fidem præsumitur non habere.
Bona fides non patitur, ut semel exactum, iterum exigatur.
Cum quid una via prohibetur alicui, ad id alia non debet admitti.
Contractus ex conventione legem accipere dignoscuntur.
Damnum quod, quis sua culpa sentit, sibi debet non aliis imputare.
Certum est, quod is committit in legem, qui legis verba complectens, contra legis nititur voluntatem.
Dat. Romæ. 5. non. Martii ipsius Bonifacii pontificatus Anno 5. Salut. Christ. 1299.
Creatus autem est Bonifacius Pontifex Maximus anno 1294. ut referunt, qui Pontificum vitas scripserunt.

page.notes: The facing page is cut off by the scan edge; its marginal notes at the right are only partly legible and were not transcribed. The word after "quando" in LXXVIII is doubtful; the printed letters look like "fuut" or "suut". The number LXXXX before "Contractus" appears printed as such; it should probably be LXXXV, but it is copied as printed. The catchword INDEX is at the right foot of the page, not in the running text.
